newsitem.title: ITALY: Omnitel sees 1996 sales of one trln lire.
newsitem.headline: Omnitel sees 1996 sales of one trln lire.

text.p: Italy's second mobile phone group Omnitel is heading for turnover of around one trillion lire in 1996, its first year of full activity, and still hopes to break even in 1998, managing director Silvio Scaglia said.
Losses this year will be "in line" with the group's budget and with first half net losses of 260 billion lire, Scaglia told reporters attending a company meeting.
The Olivetti -controlled consortium launched its GSM mobile phone service in December 1995 to compete with state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM).
Scaglia reiterated that the group considered the GSM field as its strategic business but was also interested in other possible developments.
In a company statement on Tuesday, Scaglia mentioned a possible interest in cordless phone systems using the Digital European Cordless Telephony (DECT) standard.
He said Omnitel had asked the Posts and Telecommunications ministry for authorisation to experiment with the Dect technology.
He also criticised plans by state-controlled fixed-line operator Telecom Italia to launch a cordless DECT phone service as a "violation of market laws."

Telecom Italia's announcement of its plans in October immediately sparked controversy when Italy's antitrust chairman Giuliano Amato said that if it went ahead it would be taking advantage of Telecom Italia's dominant position in the fixed line market and compete head on with mobile phone companies.
TIM has also requested authorisation to offer a cordless phone service.
Post ministry undersecretary Michele Lauria said last week the government had not yet defined the authorisation rules for cordless phones.
